content.title: What is Array Rearrangement?
content.description: Array Rearrangement refers to changing the positions of elements in an array according to specific rules or conditions without necessarily changing the data itself.

content.content: In many programming problems, we need to reorganize elements rather than simply store them. This process is called Array Rearrangement. Common examples include reversing arrays, moving zeros to the end, rotating elements, segregating positive and negative numbers, and arranging data in a specific order.

content.title: Why Rearrangement Matters
content.content: Array rearrangement techniques are widely used in sorting algorithms, scheduling systems, memory management, and optimization problems.
Array Rearrangement includes multiple operations that modify the order of elements based on a particular requirement.

items.question: Array Reversal
items.answer: Reverse the order of elements from start to end.

items.question: Array Rotation
items.answer: Move elements left or right by a fixed number of positions.

items.question: Move Zeros
items.answer: Shift all zeros to the end while maintaining relative order.

items.question: Segregation
items.answer: Group elements based on conditions such as positive/negative or even/odd.

content.content: Array reversal is one of the most common rearrangement problems. The first element swaps with the last element, the second with the second-last, and so on until the entire array is reversed.
Array rotation shifts elements either to the left or right by a specified number of positions. This operation is frequently used in circular buffers and scheduling applications.

content.title: Real Application
content.content: Rotation is used in operating systems for round-robin CPU scheduling and circular queues.
A popular interview problem involves moving all zero elements to the end of an array while maintaining the relative order of non-zero elements.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Use two pointers: one for traversing and one for placing non-zero elements.

content.content: Sometimes elements need to be rearranged based on conditions. For example, placing all negative numbers before positive numbers while preserving efficiency.

content.title: Rearranging Books on a Shelf
content.content: Imagine organizing books by subject on a shelf. The books remain the same, but their positions change to make the shelf more organized. Array rearrangement follows a similar idea.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Array Rearrangement problems are among the most commonly asked coding interview questions because they test logical thinking, optimization, and in-place manipulation skills.

items.question: Why do beginners lose data while rearranging?
items.answer: Because they overwrite elements before saving their values.

items.question: What is a common mistake in rotation problems?
Why is extra space often unnecessary?
items.answer: Many rearrangement problems can be solved using in-place techniques.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: Whenever an interview problem mentions 'without using extra space', think about two-pointer or in-place rearrangement techniques.

points: Common operations include reversal, rotation, and segregation.
